newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia rebels reject terms for soldiers' release.
newsitem.headline: Colombia rebels reject terms for soldiers' release.

text.p: Colombia's leading leftist guerrilla group on Saturday rejected government terms for the handover of 60 soldiers held prisoner for three months in a jungle-covered area of the country's southwest.

In a communique issued from somewhere in "the mountains of Colombia," the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) said the government's offer on Wednesday to demilitarize vast tracts of land in southern Caqueta province was insufficient because a key military base in the area would remain manned.
Barring the "complete withdrawal" of government troops from the area, it said, the rebels would be unable to ensure the safe handover of the prisoners to the International Committee of the Red Cross.
There was no immediate reaction from the government to the communique, which was dated Nov. 30 and sent to the NTC television news program.
The FARC, Colombia's largest and oldest rebel group, took the soldiers prisoner on Aug. 30 after overrunning the Las Delicias military base in a rural area of the southwestern province of Putumayo.

Wednesday's offer by President Ernesto Samper to demilitarize a 5,405 square-mile (14,000 square km) area for the soldiers' release, sometime between Dec. 6 and Dec. 16, had sparked hopes among desperate family members that the hostages would be home by Christmas.
